PullRequest.Title: agentHost: align relay defaults and questions with Copilot Host
PullRequest.Body:

## Summary

Align two VS Code Agent Host behaviors with Copilot Host so Copilot CLI can create and interact with sessions through Mission Control.

- Resolve omitted or empty `workingDirectories` to the relay listener's advertised `defaultDirectory`, then apply the existing authorization and filesystem-grant checks. Explicit directories still take precedence, and non-relay creation is unchanged.
- Use the request-scoped question ID `answer` for simple Copilot SDK text/single-select input requests, matching the ID Copilot Host emits and the CLI recognizes. Unique request IDs still keep concurrent responses independent. Structured elicitation forms retain their schema field IDs.
- Add regression coverage for explicit/default directory selection, denied defaults, symlink escapes, missing defaults, passive connections, non-relay behavior, and concurrent question responses; update the compatibility documentation.

Found while exercising the scenarios in [github/agent-platform#280](https://github.com/github/agent-platform/issues/280). The publishing optimization in #341404 is already merged and is not part of this diff. No CLI code or standalone CLI rendering fixes are included.

## Validation

After rebasing onto current `main`:

- `npm run build-fast -- --client-only` — passed.
- Focused tests below — **311 passed, 1 pending**.
- `npm run typecheck-client` — passed.
- `npm run eslint -- src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/protocolServerHandler.ts src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotAgentSession.ts src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/protocolServerHandler.test.ts src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotAgentSession.test.ts` — passed.
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` — passed.

```bash
./scripts/test.sh --reporter dot \
  --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/protocolServerHandler.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotAgentSession.test.ts \
  --grep 'ProtocolServerHandler|user input handling|elicitation handling'
```

Live validation on macOS with Copilot CLI 1.0.97-2 and a real Mission Control–published Code OSS host:

- Created a new session from CLI without explicit working directories; it used the advertised home directory and completed a prompt successfully.
- Rendered a single-question `answer` request in CLI, selected Blue, and verified host continuation. This verifies the compatible wire shape; the changed simple SDK callback and concurrent response routing are covered directly by unit tests.

Full smoke/integration suites were not run locally, nor were Windows/Linux live clients. The live checks preceded the rebase; the compile, focused tests, type-check, and lint were rerun afterward.

Current-head CI passed: [Code OSS](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/38491202342), including compilation/hygiene and Windows/Linux/macOS unit, integration, browser, remote, and smoke jobs; [Component Fixtures](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/38491202386); [CodeQL](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/38491202303); Telemetry, Monaco Editor checks, and chat-lib tests. The initial attempt hit an ESLint process kill (exit 137) and a macOS smoke fixture-clone network timeout before tests; both failed jobs passed on the targeted retry without code changes. Copilot review reported zero findings.

## How to Test

1. Publish a VS Code host through Mission Control, then connect Copilot CLI using `/ahp cloud <environment-id>`.
2. Select that environment with Ctrl+E and send the first prompt. Session creation should use the host's advertised default directory rather than fail with “Session creation requires a host workspace grant.”
3. Trigger a simple SDK user-input request with text or choices. The request should contain one question with ID `answer`, and CLI should render and submit it. Arbitrary structured forms remain unchanged and require a client that supports them.

(Written by Copilot)

Scenarios.Scenario: Mission Control relay creates a session without explicit workingDirectories
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The createSession JSON-RPC now resolves the advertised default directory, awaits its filesystem-grant validation, then awaits AgentService/provider session creation before replying. These checks and persistence are on the creation critical path; later Copilot SDK subprocess materialization remains deferred until first send for provisional sessions.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Canonicalize the selected default and granted roots with realpath/stat while enforcing relay filesystem grants.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One selected directory, then up to the effective granted-root count until a containing root is found.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: An omitted or empty workingDirectories list short-circuited to PermissionDenied without filesystem canonicalization; explicit one-directory requests already paid the identical validation cost.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete before session creation is authorized.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Check/register session identity and persist session/default-chat metadata.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One provider session and its fixed creation-time registry/metadata operations per create request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Omitted-directory relay requests were rejected before AgentService; explicit-directory creation already performed these operations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete before createSession returns success.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Materialize the Copilot SDK session on the first message for a provisional Copilot session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one materialization per successfully created provisional session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same deferred provider behavior applied to sessions created with an explicit directory.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the createSession critical path; it is deferred to first send.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One selected default directory per create request. Grant validation scans the effective granted-root list, whose size grows with granted roots, projects, and current session workspaces/content roots; this is the same effective cardinality as an explicit one-directory create.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Creation is sequenced per requested session ID; distinct session IDs may proceed concurrently. The diff does not alter that policy, and omitted-directory requests have the same concurrency as existing explicit-directory requests.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No new cache is added or defeated. Filesystem canonicalization is performed for the selected directory and roots on each create, as it already is for explicit directories; provider/runtime warm state is reused according to the unchanged AgentService/provider lifecycle.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed branch, grant helper, and AgentService call path are directly traced. The additional work exists only because a formerly rejected create is now intentionally allowed.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Filesystem and persistence duration depends on storage and granted-root count, but requests normally select one directory and creation is user-initiated rather than a per-message hot path.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff enables the requested session-creation workflow and gives it the same bounded authorization and creation costs as the existing explicit-directory workflow; it adds no multiplicative fan-out or concurrency increase.

Scenarios.Scenario: Mission Control relay creates a session with explicit workingDirectories
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The request validates each explicit directory and then creates the provider session, exactly as before; the new local variable forwards the same list.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Canonicalize every explicit directory against granted roots.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One validation per explicit directory, concurrently, with the same granted-root scan as before.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The base revision performed the same Promise.all validation over params.workingDirectories.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Authorization blocks provider creation until all checks finish.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create and register provider session metadata.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The number of explicit working directories after client selection; grant checks remain one per directory and provider capability may reduce unsupported multi-root configurations later.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Promise.all validates directories concurrently, unchanged by the diff; session creation remains sequenced per session ID.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache key, invalidation, coalescing, or warm/cold behavior changes for explicit directories.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: both pre- and post-diff expressions apply the same checks and URI mapping to the explicit list.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual directory/root counts vary, but this diff does not change them or their validation schedule.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance change for explicit-directory creation.

Scenarios.Scenario: Copilot SDK requests simple text or single-select user input during an active turn
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The callback constructs one in-memory ChatInputRequest, emits it to the existing state/protocol path, and awaits a renderer response keyed by the unique request ID. The response removes the pending registry entry and resolves the callback.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Publish the existing ChatInputRequested action to subscribed client/rendering surfaces and receive the existing response action.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request event and one response per SDK user-input callback.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same request/response events and payload shape were emitted, except the question key was a generated UUID.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: User response latency dominates the awaited callback; protocol publication behavior is unchanged.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One question and one pending registry entry per SDK callback; concurrent callbacks remain distinct by generated request IDs even though their single field ID is now the shared literal answer.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Concurrent requests are independent in the PendingRequestRegistry by request ID. The diff neither serializes them nor increases aggregate concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is involved. Pending entries are lifecycle state and are deleted on response or denied on turn/session cleanup.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: request IDs remain unique, pending entries are keyed and deleted by request ID, and only the nested answer field ID changed.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Callback frequency is model/tool dependent, but the changed operation replaces UUID generation with a constant string and does not increase work or retained state.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression. The change slightly reduces per-request allocation/UUID work and preserves bounded cleanup and concurrency.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed the complete five-file diff and traced both production changes through authorization, filesystem grants, AgentService/provider creation, protocol publication, concurrent request routing, and cleanup. No actionable performance regression was introduced, and the PR does not establish a shipped performance-regression fix requiring blame attribution.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
